raw_response:
I've been working this land for thirty years. I know these fields. Let me think through what I'll do this year.

My land is 10.9 mu. The way I see it, most of it — about 7.9 mu — stays in wheat and maize rotation, same as always. That rotation feeds us and gives stable income. My son and daughter-in-law work in the city now, so I can't spare as much labor for cotton as I used to. But I'm not giving it up entirely — cotton still brings better cash when the price is decent, and I know how to grow it. I'll put 3 mu into cotton, on the south plots where the soil is sandier and drains well.

For wheat, I'll plant in October after the maize comes off. I'll buy improved seeds from the township supply station, same brand I've used for five or six years — good yield, doesn't lodge. I'll apply base fertilizer before planting: mostly diammonium phosphate and some urea. I'll top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate four times — when I plant, before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I spray twice: once for herbicide in winter, once for aphids and powdery mildew in spring.

Maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June, same 7.9 mu. I'll use hybrid seed — I buy it sealed from the market. I won't plow deep, just rotary-till the stubble under. Maize gets irrigated if it's dry at sowing, then again at tasseling and grain fill. I apply fertilizer in two splits. One or two pesticide sprays — mostly herbicide early, sometimes for corn borer.

For cotton, I'll plant in late April. Hybrid cotton seed. Cotton needs more work — I'll spray six times at least, for bollworm and aphids especially. Four irrigations. I have to do this myself mostly, but I've done it alone before.
